messages:
olivia: Heads-up — discovered a divergence between the hourly GPU_seconds we use for capacity forecasts and the new per-request telemetry emitted by the runtime. low-level totals disagree by ~6% for last week. Can anyone on telemetry help reconcile before I update the dashboard?

jared: I saw that too. Seems like the runtime metric is excluding kernel prewarm time.

kevin: Prewarm +/- small, but 6% is big. Might be sampling windows differences and some requests classified as dedicated vs hosted incorrectly.

anita: @kevin can you paste the two queries? I can run a join to find the missing rows.

kevin: Sure. Runtime-derived aggregation:```sql
SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) AS hr, sum(gpu_seconds) AS runtime_gpu_sec
FROM runtime.telemetry_requests
WHERE deploy_env != 'test'
GROUP BY hr;```

kevin: Forecast pipeline aggregation:```sql
SELECT date_trunc('hour', timestamp) AS hr, sum(gpu_seconds_produced) AS forecast_gpu_sec
FROM ingest.usage_hourly
GROUP BY hr;```

jared: Noted the field name mismatch gpu_seconds_produced vs gpu_seconds. Also runtime has tags for "prewarm=true". Forecast ingestion strips that tag currently.

olivia: That explains part of it. We need to decide whether prewarm should be counted for capacity planning. My vote: include prewarm as it consumes GPUs and drives cost. Thoughts? :thinking_face: 

maya: include. ops asked for conservative headroom.

anita: Agreed. But we should make the metric names explicit in the catalog. Proposal: use metric id gpu_seconds_total (includes prewarm & kernel setup), and gpu_seconds_user (excludes prewarm/kernel). Keep both in ingest schema.

kevin: I like that. Minimal breaking change: add gpu_seconds_total to ingest, backfill for last 90 days by joining runtime telemetry and mapping prewarm tag.

olivia: Ok action items: 1) @anita add gpu_seconds_total and gpu_seconds_user to the ingest schema PR; 2) @kevin write backfill SQL and run in staging; 3) @jared update the capacity dashboard to use gpu_seconds_total for headroom charts.

jared: I'll update dashboards. Question on the backfill window — 90 days okay for forecasting models? historical seasonality needs ~180 days for winter-spring overlap.

olivia: Good catch — change to 180 days.

kevin: Backfill query draft (staging only):```sql
INSERT INTO ingest.usage_hourly (hr, gpu_seconds_total, gpu_seconds_user, source)
SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) AS hr,
       sum(case when prewarm = true then gpu_seconds else gpu_seconds end) AS gpu_seconds_total,
       sum(case when prewarm = false then gpu_seconds else 0 end) AS gpu_seconds_user,
       'runtime-telemetry'
FROM runtime.telemetry_requests
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '180 days'
GROUP BY hr;```

anita: Quick note — that CASE for gpu_seconds_total is redundant but fine for clarity. Also we need to dedupe requests that already exist in usage_hourly to avoid double counting when merging.

olivia: Add a dedupe step and run in dry-run mode first. Also create an alert if ingest lag > 2 hours during backfill.

ingest-bot: Scheduled dry-run backfill job created: dryrun-backfill-1893456789 (will write to staging table ingest.usage_hourly_backfill_staging).

maya: For the dashboard, suggest we also add a panel showing "inlet attribution" split (hosted/dedicated/private) because dedicated customers skew per-GPU utilization.

jared: Good call. I'll add that and a p95 latency / queue_time comparison so we can see skew when utilization spikes.

olivia: One more housekeeping item — metric catalog entry should include canonical name, synonyms, whether it's included in chargeback, and the data owner. @anita can you own the PR?

anita: Yep, I'll open it today. Will add tests to ensure both fields exist on ingest and the dashboard queries prefer gpu_seconds_total but can fall back to gpu_seconds_user if missing.

kevin: After dry-run looks good, I'll run the merge during a low-traffic window (Sunday 02:00 UTC) and notify infra-ops.

olivia: Thanks all. Please post the staging dry-run results here once complete. :thumbsup:
